intro.title: React Router Basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-page application with navigation between a Home page and an About page. You will learn the core concept of client-side routing, which allows your app to update the UI without a full page reload. The main technologies involved are React Router, specifically its components like BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link. You'll use TypeScript to define types for your route parameters and components, ensuring type safety throughout your application. By the end, you'll have a functional app with clickable navigation links that switch between different page components.
intro.usecase: React Router is essential for building modern single-page applications with multiple views, like e-commerce sites where users navigate between product listings, detailed product pages, shopping carts, and checkout flows without full page reloads. It's used in dashboards where different sections (analytics, user management, settings) need separate URLs for bookmarking and sharing. Social media platforms use it to handle profile pages, feeds, and messaging interfaces while maintaining browser history. Developers implement React Router whenever they need clean URL structures and seamless navigation between components that represent distinct application states or pages.
